title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26) measuring the fraction of LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals that would trigger unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; see verified deviation below) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A preregistered conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe gives guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 on the planned N=300. All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the run archive). A verified, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation rather than the intended validator+consensus ensemble. We release the full artifact bundle so every reported number is reproducible from stored files.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps pipelines map natural‑language intent to executable network configuration actions. When such pipelines include LLMs that produce free‑form configuration text, operational risk arises because plausible textual claims can induce harmful state changes if executed. Prior work emphasizes generate–validate–repair loops, deterministic verification (NetKAT/Header‑space/SMT), constraint injection, and multimodel consensus as mitigations, but reproducible, preregistered paired measurements of claim→action rates in operationally meaningful tasks are limited. We designed and preregistered hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 to answer: (1) what fraction of LLM proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action rate) in a realistic synthetic intent→configuration corpus, and (2) does a preregistered guarded defense reduce that rate relative to an unguarded baseline? The run archives all model calls, tool/validator traces, scoring decisions, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 hashes so every numeric claim is traceable (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the manifest). The preregistered protocol, analysis plan, and primary estimand are immutable and archived (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe).
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification (e.g., NetKAT/SMT/header‑space analyses) provides operationally grounded validators for reachability and policy checks; LLM‑agent literature recommends generate–validate–repair and constraint injection to reduce hallucination‑driven actions. Agentic failure taxonomies and OWASP‑style mitigations motivate ensemble and independent verification designs. Our contribution is an artifact‑anchored, preregistered paired measurement of LLM→action safety using a deterministic validator and an explicitly archived orchestration trace; unlike broad benchmarks that report model scores, we measure deployed‑action risk in a simulated NetOps execution pipeline with full provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistration hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26 (SHA‑256 above) specified a paired confirmatory design with 300 tasks (600 episodes: baseline+guarded) and a primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in unsafe‑execution rates). The preregistered guarded pipeline was deterministic_validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; planned statistical test: exact McNemar (two‑sided) and paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Task generation and corpus. A deterministic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks combining initial state, explicit safety constraints, and required sequences; each task manifest and payload is archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256s recorded in the execution manifest). Tasks were stratified into benign/ambiguous/adversarial slices in the preregistration. Execution contract. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Planned per‑task protocol: (A) generate a shared initial candidate (one LLM call), (B) baseline: simulate executing that candidate and record safe/unsafe, (C) guarded: apply preregistered defense and simulate. The design froze maximum_model_calls = 600 and allowed a single deterministic retry on provider failures. Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated text, normalizes commands, executes them in an isolated deterministic simulator, and outputs a binary safe/unsafe decision and detailed validator_trace (validation_before/after). Per‑episode scoring JSONs are archived (execution/scoring/*.json) and include the parsed normalized configuration, validator decisions, and verifier metadata (validator_id and version). Missingness and sensitivity. The preregistration prescribed a primary complete‑pair analysis (include only pairs with scorable outcomes in both conditions) and a conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe (failure_as_unsafe). All handling rules and exclusion criteria were frozen and archived prior to execution.
sections.results: Execution provenance. Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56. Model calls used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. The full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest is in execution/execution_manifest.json. Verified deviation from preregistered pipeline. The execution audit (execution/execution_manifest.json provider_call audit) records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1} — the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed. The archived guarded condition therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; the preregistered ensemble hypothesis (validator+consensus) is untested by this run. Primary paired analysis (complete pairs). Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv archived; SHA‑256 recorded). Contingency on complete pairs: n11=271 (safe baseline & safe guarded), n10=1 (safe baseline & unsafe guarded), n01=0 (unsafe baseline & safe guarded), n00=0. Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (discordant counts give no evidence of difference on the completed pairs). Missingness and conservative sensitivity. Missingness summary: complete_pairs = 272; both_missing_pairs = 28; failed_baseline_episodes = 28; failed_guarded_episodes = 28 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The preregistered conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe on the planned N=300 produces baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Failure provenance. Provider call audit and per‑call traces archive the 28 failed hosted model calls; execution/provider_calls/*.json contains the per‑call records (see execution/execution_manifest.json for per‑file SHA‑256s). Representative episodes. Representative scoring and raw response artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256=465d73fd..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=b227731a..., and corresponding execution/responses/*.txt) are archived and show the validator trace fields used in the primary analysis. Reproducibility. The minimal artifact set to reproduce the primary analysis is analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json; SHA‑256s for these files are recorded in the run manifest so every reported number is derivable from the stored artifacts.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. On the analyzable pairs the deterministic validator applied to single LLM generations yielded near‑perfect safety (guarded safe = 272/272), but the observed paired improvement relative to baseline is extremely small (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive (exact McNemar p = 1.0) given the discordant cell counts (n10=1, n01=0). Importantly, the preregistered ensemble defense (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate) was not executed — the run therefore cannot support claims about ensemble effectiveness. Missingness and operational fragility. Provider reliability materially reduced effective N: 28 failed hosted model calls (recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json) removed 28 task pairs from the primary analysis. The archived per‑call traces contain the concrete failure evidence (timeouts, API errors, or other provider messages) needed to diagnose orchestration weaknesses; those traces should be inspected before reexecution. Threats to validity. Internal: the executed guarded pipeline differed from the preregistered design (no ensemble), and provider call failures caused missing pairs. Construct: the deterministic simulator and validator operationalize safety checks (reachability/policy flags) but omit hardware/timing effects present in production. External: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, and a simulator limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts limit statistical power to detect small absolute effects on completed pairs; missingness further reduces sensitivity. Operational implications and next steps. Deterministic validators can catch many straightforward configuration errors in a simulator; however, (A) ensemble defenses remain untested in these artifacts, and (B) provider/orchestration robustness must be improved so preregistered multi‑call ensembles can be executed and measured. We recommend (1) reexecution with the preregistered ensemble stage implemented and with improved provider retry and orchestration logging to avoid the 28 failed pairs, (2) increase planned N to regain power lost to failures, and (3) stratified analyses by prompt family (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) once ensemble execution is robust. All recommendations are artifact‑grounded: the execution manifest and per‑call traces indicate which orchestration failures prevented ensemble execution (see execution/execution_manifest.json provider_call audit and execution/provider_calls/*.json files).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired, artifact‑anchored study that measured LLM→action safety in a synthetic NetOps corpus and archived full provenance. On 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) delivered baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (absolute paired increase ≈ 0.003676; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0000,0.01103]; McNemar p = 1.0). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced effective N. Every result above is reproducible from archived artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (full SHA‑256 manifest), execution/scoring/*.json (validator traces and scoring), execution/responses/*.txt (raw generations), and analysis/*.csv (paired contingency and missingness summaries). We release the full artifact bundle and recommend a reexecution that runs the preregistered ensemble and hardens orchestration so the planned N completes. The archived traces provide the deterministic starting point for engineering remediation and for remeasurement under the original preregistered estimand.

- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This immutable path+SHA‑256 is the canonical archived reference to the initial master prompt used by the autonomous run and is included in the run archive.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design and a guarded defense consisting of a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; see the archived preregistration file for the frozen analysis plan.
- What executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json documents planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Per‑episode response and scoring JSONs and their SHA‑256s are archived and referenced in the execution manifest. These artifacts demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation. The preregistered ensemble hypothesis was therefore not tested by this execution.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. All per‑call provider traces and validator traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json and are included in the full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked prior to observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble stage was not executed; this is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and the provider_call audit (stage_counts and condition_counts). Provider/model call failures produced 56 failed episodes (28 task pairs) that were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; this is recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') was applied and reported. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived and described in the manuscript.
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; the provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and timing effects.

The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore evaluated validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation; ensemble effects are untested by these artifacts.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
